segments.source: A map can be modeled with relative positions. When several moves are given, their effects can be combined rather than memorized as a picture.
Yarrow is 1 map unit(s) west of Linden; Willow is 1 map unit(s) south of Yarrow.
Treat east as +x, west as −x, north as +y, and south as −y. Add the moves in order. A fact that does not affect any coordinate is irrelevant.
Where is Willow relative to Linden? What is the straight grid displacement measured as |x|+|y|?
1. Start Linden at (0,0). 2. Translate each relation into a coordinate move. 3. Adding the moves gives (-1,-1). 4. That coordinate is south-west of Linden; the grid displacement is |-1|+|-1|=2.
Willow is south-west of Linden; grid displacement 2 unit(s).
Cardinal directions become easier to reason about when they are treated as relations that can be composed.
Grid coordinates; each statement adds a vector; sum the vectors and classify the final coordinate.
Problem 5. Position chain from Birch to Juniper
A map can be modeled with relative positions. When several moves are given, their effects can be combined rather than memorized as a picture.
Kite is 1 map unit(s) north of Birch; Alder is 1 map unit(s) east of Kite; Juniper is 1 map unit(s) south of Alder.
Treat east as +x, west as −x, north as +y, and south as −y. Add the moves in order. A fact that does not affect any coordinate is irrelevant.
Where is Juniper relative to Birch? What is the straight grid displacement measured as |x|+|y|?
1. Start Birch at (0,0). 2. Translate each relation into a coordinate move. 3. Adding the moves gives (1,0). 4. That coordinate is east of Birch; the grid displacement is |1|+|0|=1.
Juniper is east of Birch; grid displacement 1 unit(s).

Problem 6. The best route from Willow to Iris
A road map can be modeled as a graph. The best route depends on the stated criterion, not on how short it looks on paper.
Willow–Kite–Iris has segment costs [3, 4] (total 7); Willow–Oak–Northfield–Iris has segment costs [2, 2, 3] (total 7); Willow–Cedar–Iris has segment costs [6, 1] (total 7).
A route is feasible only if all of its roads are open. The cost of a route is the sum of its segment costs. Choose the feasible route with the smallest total.
Which route should a traveler use from Willow to Iris, and why?
1. List the candidate routes and their segment costs. 2. All listed routes are open. 3. Add the segment costs for every feasible route. 4. The smallest feasible total is 7, on Willow–Kite–Iris.
A shortest path is a reasoning result: first respect constraints, then compare the remaining costs.
Weighted graph; delete forbidden edges; minimize the sum of edge weights.
